# Hudson Turansky

> Independent builder of custom websites, AI tools, and software for small businesses and solo founders. Hourly, transparent pricing. Most projects ship in 2–6 weeks. AI-assisted workflows let me deliver faster and leaner than a traditional agency.

Hudson Turansky is a US-based one-person studio focused on small businesses and solo founders who need real software built well, not gated wizard templates, not bloated agency engagements. He scopes hourly, ships projects end-to-end (idea → deployed), and uses AI throughout the build to keep velocity high. He is early in client work and prices accordingly while building a track record.

## Services

- **Custom Websites**, Landing pages, business sites, and internal tools built with React, TypeScript, and modern web standards. Fast turnaround, clean code, documented on handoff.
- **Custom AI Agents and Assistants**, Personal AI assistants, company AI agents, and integrations built on Claude, Gemini, OpenAI, and MCP. Tuned to the client's data and workflow. Examples: meeting assistants that cross-reference documents in real time, document processors, research assistants, customer-support agents tied to a knowledge base.
- **Operations Software**, Custom internal applications. Admin panels, client portals, CRMs, ops dashboards. Built around how the team actually works, not a generic SaaS template.
- **Automation and Integrations**, Scripts, bots, and pipelines that connect tools and automate repetitive work. Python or Node. Common integrations: Stripe, Google Workspace, Notion, Slack, Shopify, internal CRMs.

## Process

1. **Free 30-minute discovery call.** Hudson tells you honestly whether the project is worth building, scopes it, and sends a written estimate with an hourly rate and a rough total. No commitment until both parties agree on scope.
2. **Build hourly.** Hours are tracked transparently; the client sees them as the project progresses.
3. **Ship in iterations.** Most projects deploy in 2–6 weeks; custom AI agents and operations software run longer depending on scope. Each iteration is reviewable before the next starts.
4. **Handoff with documentation.** Deployed, documented, and explained well enough that the client (or another developer) can take it forward.

## Who this is for / not for

**Good fit:**
- Small-business owners and solo founders who have an idea and need someone to actually build it.
- Non-technical buyers who want plain-language scoping and honest "is AI even the right tool here" advice.
- Contractors, professional services (legal, accounting, consulting), and e-commerce, three industries where Hudson sees the highest ROI for custom AI and operations software.
- Anyone who has been quoted by an agency and feels the price is way out of proportion to the actual scope.

**Not a fit:**
- Pre-seed startups looking for a co-founder rather than a builder.
- Projects requiring a large team (multi-person engineering, designers, PMs, separate QA).
- Anyone wanting a fixed bid before scope is locked, Hudson works hourly and scopes carefully because flat-rate quotes incentivize cutting corners.
- Anyone whose problem is already solved by a $20/month ChatGPT subscription. Hudson will tell you that on the discovery call instead of taking the money.

## FAQ

**How do I add AI to my small business?**
Start by listing the 3 most repetitive things in your week, intake forms, scheduling, email triage, document processing, customer FAQs. Then decide whether a $20 ChatGPT subscription, an off-the-shelf AI tool ($50–200/mo), or a custom build is the right level of investment. Most small businesses get the biggest first win from automating customer intake or email triage with a custom assistant tied to their own knowledge base.

**How much does custom AI cost?**
Hourly, transparent rates. A focused custom AI assistant or automation typically runs $1,500–$5,000 total. A larger custom agent that does multi-step work or operates inside an existing workflow tool usually lands $5,000–$15,000. Hudson scopes before quoting, and the client sees hours as the project progresses.

**How long does it take to build a custom AI tool?**
Most custom AI tools ship in 3–8 weeks from kickoff to deployed. A small focused automation can be done in under 2 weeks; an end-to-end custom AI agent integrated with the client's existing tools (CRM, Slack, Notion, Google Workspace) typically takes 4–8 weeks. AI-assisted workflows let Hudson build faster than a traditional agency.

**Should I hire a consultant or use ChatGPT myself?**
Use ChatGPT yourself first for everything you can, it is the cheapest test. Hire a builder when you need something embedded in your existing tools, tuned to your specific data, reliable enough to put in front of customers, or automating work across multiple steps that ChatGPT alone cannot reach. If a $20 ChatGPT subscription solves your problem, Hudson will tell you that on the discovery call.

**Do you work with contractors, professional services, or e-commerce businesses?**
Yes, those are the three buckets where Hudson sees the highest ROI for small businesses. Contractors typically need scheduling and intake automation plus document handling. Professional services (legal, accounting, consulting) need document processing and client-facing assistants. E-commerce needs custom inventory tools, customer support agents, and analytics dashboards. Different industries, similar building blocks.

**How do we get started?**
Book a free 30-minute discovery call via https://calendly.com/hudsonturansky/30min. Hudson talks through the project, tells you honestly whether it's worth building, scopes it, and sends a written estimate. No commitment until both parties agree on scope.

## Examples

- **Happy Tails Dog Walking** (Web · 2026, https://happytailsdogwalking.lovable.app), Example landing page demonstrating the kind of small-business website Hudson can ship in a single sprint. Built for demo purposes, not for an actual client.
- **Chesapeake Community Pantry** (Software · 2026, https://chesapeake-pantry.lovable.app), Example volunteer tracking OS for a food bank: shift scheduling, hour tracking, leaderboards, and manager reports. Custom internal application, the kind of operations software Hudson builds for ongoing-use teams.
- **AI Meeting Assistant** (AI · 2026), Prototype that pre-loads a stack of company documents (reports, dashboards, contracts), transcribes meetings in real time, and runs a second model in the background that cross-references what's said against the loaded context. Drops citation-backed notes when it catches misstated numbers or relevant unraised context. Demo at https://hudsonturansky.com/work, Hudson would build a real production version for a team.
